faq: Can my existing React Native app move to Expo?
Usually yes. Most apps move without trouble, and we list any libraries that need a replacement before you order. If your app has custom native code, we use Expo development builds to keep it.
Will every feature work on the web?
Most screens do. Phone-only features such as Bluetooth or some camera tools have no web equivalent, so we agree a simple fallback for each one, like a message or a file upload.
Where does the web version live?
We deploy to a host you choose, such as Vercel or Netlify, using your own account. Free tiers are enough for many apps. Hosting costs, if any, are billed to you by the host.
Do I need an Expo account?
A free Expo account is enough for builds and updates. You create it, add us as a collaborator, and we configure the project. Paid Expo plans are only needed for higher build volumes.

desc:
Expo and React Native Web app development lets one project run on iPhone, Android and in a browser. Ecom Swift LLC sets up or converts your app on Expo, adapts the screens for desktop, and configures builds so you can ship updates yourself.

## What is Expo and React Native Web?

Expo is a toolset built around React Native that handles project setup, builds and updates. React Native Web lets the same components render in a web browser. Together they let one set of screens and logic serve phones and desktop visitors.

This does not mean every feature works everywhere. Some phone features, such as certain sensors, have no browser equivalent. A good setup keeps shared code shared and handles the differences with clear, separate files.

## Why does a web version matter for a mobile app?

Many people will never install your app. A customer clicking a link in an email, a colleague on a laptop or someone searching on Google expects to open something in a browser. Without a web version, those people hit a dead end or a store page.

A web build also makes sharing easy. A link can open a specific screen, and a visitor can try the product before deciding to install. For businesses with a public catalog or booking page, that extra door can matter as much as the app itself.

## How one codebase affects cost and speed of change

Two codebases, one for the app and one for a separate website, double the work for every change. Prices, wording and rules drift apart, and bugs appear in one place but not the other.

Sharing components, navigation and a design system keeps both in step. A fix to a button style or a form rule lands everywhere. EAS Build and EAS Update shorten the path from a finished change to a test build or an over-the-air update. How much you save depends on how much of your app can be shared, which we check first.

## What a good Expo and web setup includes

- A clean Expo project with a clear folder structure and pinned versions.
- Navigation that works with browser links, the back button and refresh.
- Layouts that adapt from phone to tablet to desktop width.
- Shared components and a single design system for every platform.
- Platform-specific files only where a feature truly differs.
- Page titles and tags for public pages, so search engines can read them.
- A web deploy to a free host with a repeatable build command.
- EAS Build profiles for iOS and Android, ready to run on your own account.
- Over-the-air updates for small fixes, set up with EAS Update.
- Optional installable web app settings, so the site can sit on a phone home screen.

## What we do

We open your project and decide whether it can move to Expo directly or needs cleanup first. If you have an existing React Native app, we check which libraries are compatible and replace those that are not.

Basic gets the project running in the browser, adapts a few screens and prepares EAS Build for one platform. Standard adapts more screens, makes layouts responsive, makes deep links work and deploys the web version. Premium covers the full app, adds page tags, installable web settings, updates and a shared design system, with notes and a short call at the end.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- List the screens that must exist on the web and those that can stay mobile only.
- Decide which web pages should be public and findable.
- Keep platform checks in a few small files rather than scattered through the code.
- Test in a desktop browser and on a real phone browser.
- Create your own Expo account so you own builds and updates.

**Avoid:**
- Promising every phone feature on the web.
- Copying phone layouts onto wide screens without changes.
- Hiding public content behind a login when it should be searchable.
- Pushing over-the-air updates that change native code.
- Mixing app and web analytics without labeling them.

## Who this service is for

A mobile app owner who wants a browser version for customers without a phone app. A startup that needs a marketing page and a product demo from the same code. A team with a messy Expo or React Native project that cannot run on the web today.

## What we need from you

Repository access as a collaborator, a list of the screens you want on the web and the domain or host you plan to use. If you already have an Expo account, add us as a team member. We never need passwords, and we reply with a short checklist after you order.
